narrative:
The model estimates a 68% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Having received other job opportunities while at your company was the strongest influence, pushing the model strongly toward expecting you to leave. Employees predicted to stay rarely report receiving such external offers, making this a significant signal of potential departure.

Your 6–10 years of experience in your current role was the second most important factor, but this actually worked in your favor by pulling the prediction slightly toward staying. Most employees the model expects to remain have shorter tenures of 1–5 years, so your longer current tenure signals some stability.

Your overall career experience of more than 11 years ranked third and pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many who are expected to stay have only 1–5 years of total experience, your extensive background appears to indicate stronger external prospects.

Taken together, these elements suggest the organization sees you as someone with attractive outside options despite your solid time with them. You and your manager should discuss ways to strengthen your sense of commitment and address any unmet needs—such as recognition, better support, or clearer growth paths—to reduce the risk of you leaving. Exploring internal opportunities that match what external roles might offer could also help retain you. (248 words)
